claims.claim: Since 2012, Malaysian courts must order convicts to compensate their victims when prosecutors ask.
claims.source: Attorney General's Chambers, Criminal Procedure Code, updated text as at 4 July 2023, s.426(1A) and amendment table: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1841142_BI/Act%20593%20-%20Muktamad%20as%20at%204.7.23%20(1.12.23)%20(2).pdf.
claims.correction: Correct for the current mandatory-on-application structure, subject to the statutory conditions. An order does not establish actual payment.
claims.stale_check: The subsequent amendments examined do not change s.426.

claims.claim: CPC s.426(1A). The court sets the sum, weighs the convict's ability to pay, and orders it only for the victim of the convicted offence.
claims.source: AGC, Criminal Procedure Code, 4 July 2023, ss.426(1A)-(1C): https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1841142_BI/Act%20593%20-%20Muktamad%20as%20at%204.7.23%20(1.12.23)%20(2).pdf.
claims.correction: The amount and connection to the convicted offence require determination; compensation is not automatically the victim's entire claimed loss.

claims.claim: The court weighs listed factors including 'the ability of the convicted accused to pay' (s.426(1C)(f)) and may hold an inquiry (s.426(1D)).
claims.source: AGC, Criminal Procedure Code, 4 July 2023, s.426(1C)(f) and s.426(1D), p.234: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1841142_BI/Act%20593%20-%20Muktamad%20as%20at%204.7.23%20(1.12.23)%20(2).pdf.

claims.claim: The AGC text records s.426 as last amended by Acts A1378 and A1422, both in force on 1 June 2012; later CPC amendments (A1692, A1722, A1751) leave s.426 untouched.
claims.source: AGC CPC amendment table, 4 July 2023; Act A1422, gazetted 9 February 2012: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/853_BI/Act%20A1422.pdf; Act A1692, gazetted 11 August 2023: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1845385_BI/A1692%20BI.pdf; Act A1722, gazetted 25 September 2024: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2368175_BI/Act%20A1722.pdf; Act A1751, gazetted 7 March 2025: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2731057_BI/Criminal%20Procedure%20Code%20(Amendment)%20Act%202025%20A1751.pdf.
claims.correction: The official amendment table supports the commencement date. The original enacted text of A1378 was not independently retrieved.
claims.stale_check: The cited later Acts were examined directly; none amends s.426.

claims.claim: CPC Reprint 2006 has no s.426(1A)
claims.source: Commissioner of Law Revision, official Criminal Procedure Code reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 January 2006, s.426, p.177; copy hosted by the International Commission of Jurists: https://www.icj.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/01/Malaysia-Criminal-Procedure-Code-1935-1999-eng.pdf.
claims.correction: The older s.426(1)(b) nevertheless permitted discretionary compensation. June 2012 was not the first availability of criminal-court compensation.
claims.stale_check: This is a historical comparison, not a description of the current provision.

claims.claim: The statute text says 'Public Prosecution' in s.426(1A); cards say 'prosecutors'.
claims.source: AGC, Criminal Procedure Code, 4 July 2023, s.426(1A): https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1841142_BI/Act%20593%20-%20Muktamad%20as%20at%204.7.23%20(1.12.23)%20(2).pdf.

claims.claim: On 15 Apr 2026, Attorney General Dusuki Mokhtar ordered prosecutors to apply for compensation orders for crime victims, FMT reported.
claims.source: No original AGC directive, circular or official transcript was located. FMT's report is dated 15 April 2026: https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2026/04/15/dpps-ordered-to-seek-compensation-for-crime-victims. The originating Berita Harian publisher archive, also dated 15 April, describes a directive that would be issued: https://www.klik.com.my/item/story/31830693/Untitled. These establish the media accounts, not formal issuance.
claims.correction: FMT did report an order. However, the official directive's existence, issuance date and operative wording remain independently unverified. The upstream account uses future tense. Write 'FMT reported on 15 April that the AG had instructed prosecutors' and preserve the verification limitation.
claims.stale_check: The conflicting formulations are contemporaneous April reports, both predating the 7 November editor check. No subsequent official issuance was verified.

claims.claim: It covers crime victims, drink-driving deaths included, 'in the appropriate cases'.
claims.source: No primary text of the AG's announcement or directive was obtained. Secondary account: FMT, 15 April 2026, https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2026/04/15/dpps-ordered-to-seek-compensation-for-crime-victims.
claims.correction: This faithfully describes FMT's reported scope, but cannot be upgraded to independently verified official policy. Retain the appropriate-cases qualification wherever the scope is summarized.
claims.stale_check: The evidential limitation already existed at the 7 November 2026 editor check.

claims.claim: He said it was not conventional practice and not possible in all cases.
claims.source: No original speech or official transcript was located. FMT English, 15 April 2026: https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2026/04/15/dpps-ordered-to-seek-compensation-for-crime-victims. FMT Malay: https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/bahasa/tempatan/2026/04/15/peguam-negara-wajibkan-tpr-mohon-pampasan-terhadap-keluarga-mangsa-jenayah.
claims.correction: The English article supports this reported-speech attribution. The Malay account instead describes applications not being implemented comprehensively across cases. Incomplete implementation and impossibility are different propositions; the original words are needed to resolve the difference.
claims.stale_check: This is a contemporaneous reporting or translation issue, not an identified later policy change.

claims.claim: The directive is general, not scam-specific.
claims.source: Original directive unavailable. FMT, 15 April 2026: https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2026/04/15/dpps-ordered-to-seek-compensation-for-crime-victims.
claims.correction: The media report discusses crime victims generally and includes drink-driving deaths. Describe that as the reported announcement's scope; formal operative scope remains unverified.
claims.stale_check: Checked as at 8 November 2026; no verified later change resolves the missing primary document.

claims.claim: The provision the directive switches on is s.426(1A)
claims.source: Government response to SUHAKAM's 2019 annual report, published 2021, pp.128-129, already discusses s.426 compensation: https://suhakam.org.my/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/maklumbalas-kerajaan2019.pdf.
claims.correction: The provision was already operative. An instruction could change prosecutorial practice, but does not activate previously unavailable statutory authority.
claims.stale_check: The relevant authority and official discussion predate April 2026.

claims.claim: Malaysia's scam response centre returned RM7.3m of the RM25.2m it seized from 2022 to 2025: 29%, the Home Ministry told Parliament.
claims.source: Primary corroboration for the amounts: Home Ministry written answer, 4 February 2026, question 82, https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/jindex/pdf/JDR04022026.pdf. It reports cumulative RM25.24m seized and RM7.33m returned since 2022. The precise June reply and its stated 2022-2025 cutoff were not retrieved. Secondary June report: https://www.bernama.com/en/news.php/general/news.php?id=2572390.
claims.correction: The amounts are independently supported at greater precision, and 7.33/25.24 is approximately 29.04%. The retrieved February passage does not explicitly identify 31 December 2025 as the cumulative cutoff. The full claim remains unverified specifically on that reporting window and June attribution, not because the amounts have been disproved.
claims.stale_check: Later cumulative figures do not invalidate a correctly dated historical snapshot.

claims.claim: From January to May 2026 it returned RM3.57m of RM7.25m seized, or 49%.
claims.source: Original parliamentary reply not obtained. Secondary reports dated 24 June 2026: Bernama, https://www.bernama.com/en/news.php/general/news.php?id=2572390; The Star, https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/06/24/billions-lost-to-scams-since-2022-but-only-rm109mil-returned-dewan-rakyat-told.
claims.correction: The reports agree and the arithmetic is correct: 3.57/7.25 is approximately 49.24%. Agreement between reports does not independently verify their shared underlying reply. Nor does this ratio establish that 49% of victims, or 49% of all scam losses, were reimbursed.
claims.stale_check: The later January-June figures concern a different window and cannot alone disprove this January-May claim.

claims.claim: In a written reply posted on the Parliament portal on 24 June 2026 (to Ronald Kiandee, PN), the Home Ministry said the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) had seized RM32.49 million of fraud victims' funds since it was set up in 2022 and returned RM10.9 million.
claims.source: The original June answer and portal posting metadata were not obtained. Secondary sources: Bernama, 24 June 2026, https://www.bernama.com/en/news.php/general/news.php?id=2572390; The Star, 24 June 2026, https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/06/24/billions-lost-to-scams-since-2022-but-only-rm109mil-returned-dewan-rakyat-told. Primary earlier totals: https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/jindex/pdf/JDR04022026.pdf.
claims.correction: The totals are arithmetically compatible with the more precise earlier figures: 25.24 + 7.25 = 32.49 and 7.33 + 3.57 = 10.90. This reconciliation does not verify the later inputs. Distinguish the reply's date from its publication date: The Star describes a 23 June reply, which could have been posted or reported on 24 June.
claims.stale_check: No numerical contradiction is established by the different displayed rounding or publication dates.

claims.claim: Returns through its earmarking process rose from RM508,479.39 in 2024 to RM6.65m in 2025.
claims.source: Home Ministry written answer, 4 February 2026, question 82: https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/jindex/pdf/JDR04022026.pdf.
claims.correction: The annual returned amounts are confirmed. Earmarking identifies or restricts funds; subsequent legal processes enable their return. It should not be described as itself paying victims.
claims.stale_check: The later July oral figures differ slightly; that discrepancy is recorded under omitted_facts.

claims.claim: On 3 March 2026 Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the NSRC recorded 'a significant surge in returning funds to victims through the earmarking process, rising from RM508,479.39 in 2024 to RM6.65mil in 2025'.
claims.source: NFCC confirms the 3 March 2026 inauguration and handover: https://nfcc.jpm.gov.my/index.php/ms/aktiviti/majlis-perasmian-dan-penyerahan-pusat-respons-penipuan-kebangsaan-nsrc. KDN's official index lists a relevant statement dated 3 March, but its body was not retrieved: https://www.moha.gov.my/utama/index.php/ms/saluran-maklumat/hebahan/kenyataan-media. The amounts are independently supported by the 4 February parliamentary answer.
claims.correction: The event and annual amounts have primary support. The precise quotation and attribution to Saifuddin on that date remain dependent on media reporting. An indexed statement title is not evidence of its unavailable contents.
claims.stale_check: All identified supporting records predate the editor check; this remains a quotation-verification gap.

claims.claim: RM14.01 million returned from 12 Oct 2022 to Aug 2026 (written reply, 3 Nov 2026)
claims.source: Original 3 November parliamentary reply not retrieved. Secondary report: Malay Mail, 4 November 2026, https://www.malaymail.com/amp/news/malaysia/2026/11/04/scam-victims-recover-just-1pc-of-rm123b-lost-over-past-decade-parliament-told/241910.
claims.correction: Retain as an attributed, unverified figure until the original answer is available. Its being below the September total is chronologically plausible, but plausibility does not verify it.
claims.stale_check: The article predates the 7 November editor check. A later publication can legitimately report an earlier cutoff.

claims.claim: RM14.3 million to Sep 2026 (27 Oct 2026)
claims.source: Official Dewan Rakyat digital Hansard, 27 October 2026: https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-rakyat/2026-10-27. It reports RM14.3m returned from 12 October 2022 through September 2026.
claims.correction: Confirmed as the minister's reported cumulative amount. The retrieved digital transcript is marked draft.
claims.stale_check: The September cutoff, rather than the reporting date, governs comparisons with the August figure.

claims.claim: Later cumulative figures run on the same pool
claims.source: The October parliamentary statement is available: https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-rakyat/2026-10-27. Original June and November replies and a common methodological reconciliation were not obtained.
claims.correction: The reported totals increase in cutoff-date order, but that does not establish identical definitions, case coverage or revision treatment. Describe them as reported cumulative NSRC totals with different cutoffs, rather than a fully reconciled series.
claims.stale_check: This is a comparability limitation, not evidence that one total became wrong after publication.

claims.claim: They exclude bank compensation under BNM's SEFT policy, magistrates' delivery orders under CPC s.413 and court-ordered returns such as Agrobank's RM1.505m (21 Sep 2026).
claims.source: KDN's government channel, reporting an NSRC/PDRM infographic for October 2022-September 2026, explicitly identifies RM14,267,443.95 as returns under s.413: https://t.me/s/kementeriandalamnegeri?q=%23kdn. Home Ministry's 3 March 2026 parliamentary answer also describes earmarking, seizure and court-directed return as stages of the NSRC process: https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/jindex/pdf/JDR03032026.pdf.
claims.correction: The exclusion of s.413 returns is contradicted by official reporting. NSRC is an operational channel; s.413 is a legal mechanism used within it. The evidence does not establish whether the particular Agrobank order or any SEFT payments are included in these totals. Those boundaries remain unverified.
claims.stale_check: The relevant official evidence predates the 7 November editor check. No subsequent change is needed to explain this error.

claims.claim: court-ordered returns such as Agrobank's RM1.505m (21 Sep 2026)
claims.source: No original court order or judgment was obtained. Secondary report: The Edge, 21 September 2026, https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/818740.
claims.correction: The report describes an order for RM1.505m to be returned to Agrobank from 60 mule accounts. It concerns the bank's own lost funds, and an order is not proof of completed payment. Neither the order nor exclusion from NSRC totals was independently verified.
claims.stale_check: Any later execution of the order could change payment status; no primary execution record was located as at 8 November.

claims.claim: on 27 Jan 2026 he gave RM6.7m and called the sums 'diselamatkan' (saved).
claims.source: Official Dewan Rakyat Hansard, 27 January 2026, pp.31-32: https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/hindex/pdf/DR-27012026.pdf. The same exchange explicitly clarifies RM6.7m as returned to victims, distinguishing it from funds saved and seized.
claims.correction: The initial use of 'saved' is selectively reported. The subsequent clarification makes clear that RM6.7m referred to money returned. Prefer the more precise written annual figure if desired, but do not justify that choice by treating RM6.7m as a different saved-money measure.
claims.stale_check: The clarification was in the same January sitting, long before the editor check.

claims.claim: both are the same pool.
claims.source: January figure: official Hansard, 27 January 2026, https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/hindex/pdf/DR-27012026.pdf. More precise annual figure: written answer, 4 February 2026, https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/jindex/pdf/JDR04022026.pdf.
claims.correction: Both refer broadly to 2025 NSRC returns. However, no primary reconciliation establishes that RM6.7m and RM6.65m use precisely identical records or explains the difference. Do not assert an exact reconciliation solely from their proximity.
claims.stale_check: The variation existed in the original January-February reporting.

claims.claim: The Home Ministry's RM2.97b of 2025 online-fraud losses is a different pool
claims.source: The original Home Ministry answer supporting RM2.97b was not retrieved. BNM's Annual Report 2025, released 31 March 2026, reports RM2.8b of online-fraud losses using PDRM data: https://www.bnm.gov.my/publications/ar2025/box4.
claims.correction: Reported losses and seized funds are different measures. The specific RM2.97b total remains unverified. Report the alternative primary RM2.8b figure and seek definitions, revision dates and coverage before treating the two as contradictory. BNM's directly available description is preferable for a sourced claim within its stated scope.
claims.stale_check: The later alleged June total could reflect a revision or different scope, but neither explanation has been established.

claims.claim: RM34.05m saved in 2025
claims.source: BNM Annual Report 2025, p.97, provides approximately RM34m earmarked in 2025: https://www.bnm.gov.my/documents/20124/21185005/ar2025_en_ch1g.pdf. The exact RM34.05m appears in March media reports, but the relevant KDN release body was not obtained.
claims.correction: Primary evidence supports the approximate scale, not this exact precision and wording. Preserve BNM's earmarked label when using its figure. Earmarking does not itself establish payment to victims or final recovery.
claims.stale_check: This is a precision and metric-verification issue, not an identified later change.

claims.claim: RM19m in freezing orders
claims.source: BNM Annual Report 2025, p.97, NSRC diagram: https://www.bnm.gov.my/documents/20124/21185005/ar2025_en_ch1g.pdf. Released 31 March 2026.
claims.correction: State approximately RM19m and specify the 2025 reporting window. Freezing orders are not completed victim reimbursements.
claims.stale_check: A historical annual figure; later totals do not supersede its stated window.

claims.claim: RM100.93m prevented
claims.source: Official Dewan Rakyat digital Hansard, 27 October 2026: https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-rakyat/2026-10-27. The minister identifies RM100.93m as earmarked, with further processes pending.
claims.correction: Use 'RM100.93m earmarked', with the stated procedural qualification. The whole amount cannot be presented as established prevented losses. This does not mean no losses were prevented; the error is the unsupported metric label.
claims.stale_check: The primary statement predates the 7 November editor check.

claims.claim: RM1.2b attempted fraud prevented
claims.source: BNM Governor's IFCTF speech, 6 October 2026: https://alumni.bnm.gov.my/web/guest/-/g-spch-ifctf26.
claims.correction: Specify that this is attempted fraud prevented by the financial sector in 2025. It is not an NSRC victim-return total. A similarly sized NSRC reported-loss figure elsewhere concerns a different measure and period.
claims.stale_check: The 2025 amount remains a historical figure even though the same speech reports newer prevention activity.

claims.claim: Bank Negara counted 969 convictions of mule account holders in 2025.
claims.source: BNM Annual Report 2025, Maintaining Financial Integrity, p.97, released 31 March 2026: https://www.bnm.gov.my/documents/20124/21185005/ar2025_en_ch1g.pdf.
claims.correction: Use 'BNM reported 969 convictions against mule account holders'. The passage does not establish 969 unique people, 969 separate cases, an offence-by-offence breakdown, or compensation outcomes.
claims.stale_check: The figure concerns 2025 and should not be presented as a post-April-2026 outcome.

claims.claim: Penal Code ss.424A to 424D (Act A1721) and CPC amendments in force from 30 October 2024.
claims.source: AGC, Act A1721, gazetted 25 September 2024: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2368163_BI/Act%20A1721.pdf; Act A1722: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2368175_BI/Act%20A1722.pdf. The 30 October commencement is confirmed in official Dewan Rakyat Hansard, 18 November 2024: https://repositori.parlimen.gov.my/bitstream/123456789/1736/22/DR-18112024.
claims.correction: The enactments and commencement date are supported. This does not establish that every conviction in BNM's aggregate was under the newly inserted provisions.
claims.stale_check: Historical commencement evidence predates the 2025 conviction cohort.

claims.source: The exact commencement notice bearing this identifier was not independently retrieved. The commencement date is separately supported by official Hansard, 18 November 2024: https://repositori.parlimen.gov.my/bitstream/123456789/1736/22/DR-18112024.
claims.correction: Keep the verified commencement date separate from the unverified gazette identifier. Obtain the original notice before retaining the identifier as independently checked.
claims.stale_check: A historical document-verification gap, not a later legal change.

claims.claim: cheating (Penal Code s.420)
claims.source: AGC, Penal Code updated text as at 31 May 2023, s.420: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1823715_BI/Act%20574%20Project%202%20Final.pdf.
claims.correction: For precise data requests, identify s.420 as cheating involving dishonest inducement to deliver property or deal with valuable security. It is not the only cheating provision.

claims.claim: mule-account (ss.424A to 424D)
claims.source: AGC, Penal Code (Amendment) Act 2024, Act A1721, gazetted 25 September 2024: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/2368163_BI/Act%20A1721.pdf.
claims.correction: The range describes the legislative framework, but is imprecise in a request for offence or prosecution counts. Sections 424A-424C create offences; s.424D supplies definitions and is not a separate chargeable offence.
claims.stale_check: This distinction appears in the original 2024 amendment.

claims.claim: All came before the April 2026 directive.
claims.source: BNM Annual Report 2025, p.97, establishes that the convictions occurred in 2025: https://www.bnm.gov.my/documents/20124/21185005/ar2025_en_ch1g.pdf.
claims.correction: The chronology is correct relative to the reported April 2026 announcement. Write 'The 2025 convictions predate the reported April 2026 announcement', because formal directive issuance remains separately unverified.
claims.stale_check: Nothing about the later announcement establishes that compensation applications were unavailable or absent in 2025.

claims.claim: '20 individuals from 51 cases' charged under s.424A (27 Jan 2026).
claims.source: Official Dewan Rakyat Hansard, 27 January 2026, p.31: https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/hindex/pdf/DR-27012026.pdf.
claims.correction: The parliamentary sequence supports 20 of 51 reported s.424A cases having reached charges. It does not clearly establish 20 distinct individuals. This narrower offence and prosecution-stage count is not directly comparable with BNM's 969 convictions.
claims.stale_check: The unit ambiguity was present in the January record; no later change explains it.

claims.claim: No published count shows how often they ask in scam cases.
claims.source: No primary source establishing universal non-publication was found. Sampled official publications include Judiciary statistics for September 2026, https://www.kehakiman.gov.my/sites/default/files/09-portal-unit-statistics-bm_bi-september-2026.pdf, and December 2025, https://www.kehakiman.gov.my/sites/default/files/12.%20Portal%20Unit%20Statistics%20BM_BI%20%20Disember%202025.pdf. They do not supply the requested application breakdown.
claims.correction: Replace with 'No publicly available aggregate count of these applications was located in the sources searched as at 8 November 2026.' A search result cannot establish that no count exists anywhere or that prosecutors never apply.
claims.stale_check: No evidence was found of an intervening publication between the 7 November editor check and this review.

claims.claim: No published count shows how many ended with a compensation order.
claims.source: BNM's report gives the 969 convictions without a compensation breakdown: https://www.bnm.gov.my/documents/20124/21185005/ar2025_en_ch1g.pdf. Sampled Judiciary statistics likewise lack this breakdown: https://www.kehakiman.gov.my/sites/default/files/09-portal-unit-statistics-bm_bi-september-2026.pdf. No official confirmation of universal non-publication was obtained.
claims.correction: State that no linked compensation-order count was located for this cohort. Do not infer zero orders or assume every conviction was an eligible compensation case.
claims.stale_check: The negative finding is bounded by the publications examined through 8 November 2026.

claims.claim: No court ruling was found on whether a scam victim counts as the victim of a mule account offence.
claims.source: No retrieved judgment resolved this precise question. The relevant statutory condition is in CPC s.426(1A): https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1841142_BI/Act%20593%20-%20Muktamad%20as%20at%204.7.23%20(1.12.23)%20(2).pdf.
claims.correction: The bounded 'no ruling was found' wording is defensible as a research disclosure. Do not shorten it to 'untested' or infer either automatic eligibility or categorical ineligibility.
claims.stale_check: Public searches through 8 November cannot exclude unpublished or unindexed lower-court orders.

claims.claim: The government counts and publishes the NSRC route (previous card), so the gap is specific to court compensation orders.
claims.source: Official NSRC reporting includes s.413 returns: https://t.me/s/kementeriandalamnegeri?q=%23kdn. The October parliamentary statement publishes an aggregate returned amount: https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-rakyat/2026-10-27.
claims.correction: The demonstrated gap is a publicly located aggregate breakdown of s.426 applications, orders and payments. NSRC reporting already includes a court-mediated return mechanism. It is inaccurate to contrast NSRC with all court-based recovery, and no comprehensive audit establishes that reporting gaps exist only in s.426.
claims.stale_check: The overlap is established by evidence available before the editor check.

claims.claim: It does not publish how often its courts order convicted offenders to pay victims.
claims.source: No authoritative statement confirming nationwide non-publication was located. Sampled official court statistics: https://www.kehakiman.gov.my/sites/default/files/09-portal-unit-statistics-bm_bi-september-2026.pdf.
claims.correction: This categorical national claim exceeds the evidence. Use 'The reviewed publications did not provide an aggregate count of s.426 compensation orders.' The same correction applies to the headline suggestion.
claims.stale_check: No verified recent change explains the overstatement; the problem is the inference from a limited search.

claims.claim: Until someone publishes how often they ask, the public cannot tell whether that law works.
claims.source: No primary evaluation establishes this absolute claim. CPC s.426(4) distinguishes sums actually paid from an order's existence: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1841142_BI/Act%20593%20-%20Muktamad%20as%20at%204.7.23%20(1.12.23)%20(2).pdf.
claims.correction: Missing aggregate data limits evaluation. Application counts alone are insufficient: eligible cases, orders, amounts, actual payments and enforcement outcomes also matter.
claims.stale_check: This is an unsupported evaluative inference rather than a claim made stale by a later event.

claims.claim: on BNM's application
claims.source: AGC, Act 613 updated as at 1 March 2026, s.83D: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/3285881_BI/Act%20613%20(Online%202026).pdf. BNM's official explanation of its competent-authority role: https://amlcft.bnm.gov.my/bank-negara-malaysia-as-the-competent-authority.
claims.correction: BNM can apply in its competent-authority capacity, but it is not the only applicant contemplated: the provision also covers the relevant regulatory or supervisory authority. The power is discretionary, concerns AMLA contraventions, and is not a general compensation entitlement for every scam victim.
claims.stale_check: The operative 2026 text was checked.

claims.claim: no reported use, untested for scam victims
claims.source: No primary case record or official usage inventory establishing these negative claims was located. The statute confirms the power, not its usage history: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/3285881_BI/Act%20613%20(Online%202026).pdf.

omitted_facts: Compensation authority predates 2012: the official 2006 CPC reprint already contained discretionary compensation under s.426(1)(b). CPC s.426(1B) addresses payment through representatives for deceased victims and parents or guardians for children. Section 426(4) preserves civil recovery beyond compensation actually paid. These provisions reinforce the need to distinguish eligibility, orders and completed payment. Source: AGC CPC, 4 July 2023, https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1841142_BI/Act%20593%20-%20Muktamad%20as%20at%204.7.23%20(1.12.23)%20(2).pdf.

The NSRC process can move from earmarking to seizure under s.116D and then court-directed return. A 3 March 2026 Home Ministry written answer describes that sequence. Thus administrative program totals and legal mechanisms overlap. Source: question 66, https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/jindex/pdf/JDR03032026.pdf.

BNM's SEFT compensation framework concerns unauthorized transactions and excludes customer-authorized transfers induced by scams. BNM reports approximately 26% more victims receiving full or partial compensation in 2025 than in 2024, but that relative increase is not an absolute national compensation count or amount. Sources: BNM Annual Report 2025, https://www.bnm.gov.my/publications/ar2025/box4; policy announcement, 28 June 2024, https://alumni.bnm.gov.my/web/guest/-/pd-fair-treatment24.

Official annual figures are not perfectly consistent across publications. The 21 July 2026 Senate draft transcript gives 2024 seizures of RM7.5m and returns of RM508,478, and 2025 seizures of RM17.4m and returns of RM6.6m. The 4 February written answer gives RM7.26m/RM508,479.39 and RM17.49m/RM6.65m respectively. Rounding, revision, scope or transcription could contribute, but the cause was not established. Prefer the explicit written annual figures for precision while disclosing the alternatives. Sources: https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-negara/2026-07-21?search=undefined and https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/jindex/pdf/JDR04022026.pdf.

The same 21 July 2026 Senate transcript reports January-June 2026 seizures of RM7.2m and returns of RM4.1m, or 57%. This is a later and different reporting window from January-May, and should not be silently substituted for it. Source: https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-negara/2026-07-21?search=undefined.

A KDN publication for October 2022-September 2026 reports RM98,583,385.05 earmarked, RM34,863,780.41 seized under s.116D and RM14,267,443.95 returned under s.413. Its earmarked amount differs from the minister's RM100.93m parliamentary statement. No reconciliation was found. Use the parliamentary figure when reporting that statement and disclose the alternative official amount; do not combine them into an assumed consistent series. Sources: https://t.me/s/kementeriandalamnegeri?q=%23kdn and https://hansard.parlimen.gov.my/hansard/dewan-rakyat/2026-10-27.

The retrieved return and seizure totals are aggregate amounts. They do not supply a matched case cohort showing what proportion of a particular set of seizures was ultimately returned, or what proportion of victims received full reimbursement. The 29% and reported 49% ratios should therefore remain narrowly described as returned-over-seized amounts for their stated reporting windows. Primary example: Home Ministry written answer, 4 February 2026, https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/jindex/pdf/JDR04022026.pdf.

The 3 March 2026 NSRC inauguration and handover should not be treated as the start of continuous operations. The Home Ministry's parliamentary answer states that the 24-hour one-stop operation began on 26 June 2025. Sources: https://www.parlimen.gov.my/files/jindex/pdf/JDR03032026.pdf and the NFCC event record, https://nfcc.jpm.gov.my/index.php/ms/aktiviti/majlis-perasmian-dan-penyerahan-pusat-respons-penipuan-kebangsaan-nsrc.
source_assessment: The supplied core bibliography identifies approximately 14 publications or records: seven legislative texts or metadata records, one BNM annual report, and six media articles. These are not 14 independent evidential sources. Bernama republication, articles describing the same parliamentary answer, the FMT account derived from Berita Harian, and HTML/PDF versions of one report share underlying origins. The substantive institutional perspective is overwhelmingly governmental or regulatory: AGC, Parliament/Home Ministry, the Judiciary and BNM. Ronald Kiandee appears as an opposition questioner, but the analysis does not include developed opposition analysis, victim testimony, independent legal expertise, academic evaluation, NGO evidence or banking-sector operational evidence. Government primary sources are appropriate and usually decisive for statutory wording and official statistics; political balance is not required to establish what a statute says. The material weakness is incomplete primary verification of the reported directive, several parliamentary answers, the Agrobank order and categorical absence claims. The diversity estimate of 0.35 is qualitative, not a statistical measurement. The internal briefs were unavailable, and repeated research passes were not counted as independent primary corroboration.
overall_assessment: Reviewed as at 8 November 2026 against the analysis's 7 November 2026 editor check. The statutory foundation is substantially sound: the present s.426 structure, its principal qualifications and the June 2012 amendment history are supported, as are BNM's 969 convictions, the annual RM508,479.39/RM6.65m return figures and the September cumulative RM14.3m statement. However, the analysis needs substantive correction before publication. Its clearest error is excluding s.413 returns from NSRC totals; the official reporting explicitly includes them. It also mislabels RM100.93m as prevented losses, selectively characterizes January's RM6.7m as merely saved, and turns unsuccessful searches into categorical claims of non-publication. The official AG directive, exact June and November reply details, Agrobank order and several ancillary assertions remain unverified under the requested primary-source standard. Unverified does not mean false. The score of 70 is a qualitative assessment of factual reliability and publication readiness, not a measured percentage of false claims. Repeated substantive claims in the hook, cards, headline, context and notes have been consolidated; editorial choices and unprovided workflow assertions are not treated as independent evidence. All four cardinal-sin categories were considered, but no additional UNDERCLAIM was established strongly enough to flag. The documented corrections rely on evidence predating the editor check, so they are not explained by an identified overnight change.
